etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English brouken (“to use, enjoy”), from Old English brūcan (“to enjoy, brook, use, possess, partake of, spend”), from Proto-West Germanic *brūkan, from Proto-Germanic *brūkaną (“to enjoy, use”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰruHg- (“to enjoy”).
Cognate with Saterland Frisian bruke (“to need”), Dutch bruiken (“to use”), German Low German bruken (“to need”), German brauchen (“to need”), Swedish bruka (“to use”), Icelandic brúka (“to use”).
senses: (formal, chiefly in the negative) To bear; endure; put up with; tolerate.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: From Middle English brook, from Old English brōc (“brook; stream; torrent”), from Proto-West Germanic *brōk (“stream”).
senses: (chiefly Northeastern US, parts of UK) A body of running water smaller than a river; a small stream.
